transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Torres (Calypso Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Calypso Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (Calypso CTO)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private, SDK support (Python/Node), connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Customer is evaluating for a hybrid rollout (hosted for dev, dedicated for production) and has strict observability and SSO requirements.

Topics: integration patterns, SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, rate limits, observability/tracing, security/compliance

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll just do quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the infra team.
[00:07] Janelle Torres: Hi, I'm Janelle, I head up ML. Sorry about the noise in the background.
[00:12] Marco Ruiz: Marco here, platform engineering, I'll be hands-on with any deployment.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: Aisha, CTO — we'll be listening in for architecture and security questions.
[00:20] Liam Patel: Liam Patel, solutions engineer, I'll cover integration + SDK questions.
[00:24] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda, we want to understand your current stack, what you're trying to build, and the integration constraints — then we'll talk about patterns (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and answer any questions.
[00:34] Janelle Torres: High level — we're building an in-store assistant for associates, also a shopper-facing chat on mobile. Latency is fairly important for the in-store flow, like 200–300ms target on short queries. Cost matters too; we have heavy peak traffic during promos.
[00:47] Marco Ruiz: Our infra — mostly AWS, uses EKS, internal auth via Okta SAML, datadog for observability. We have a gateway (NGINX/Envoy) and an API layer in Node, and a small Python ML stack for some workflows.
[01:02] Maya Chen: Great, that helps. Do you have preference for hosted to start or private from day one?
[01:07] Aisha Khan: We'd like to pilot hosted for speed but need a clear migration path to dedicated or VPC-private later.
[01:13] Liam Patel: That's a common pattern — hosted for dev, dedicated reserved capacity for production. The API is the same; you pin model versions and rollout policies.
[01:22] Janelle Torres: On integration — what SDKs do you have? We use LangChain in some experiments and LlamaIndex in a few PoCs.
[01:29] Liam Patel: We have official SDKs: python and node SDKs, and they support streaming, function calling, and structured outputs. We also have connectors and example code for LangChain and LlamaIndex — basically wrappers that map Redwood API calls into the chain/run abstractions.
[01:43] Janelle Torres: Are those first-party maintained?
[01:45] Liam Patel: Yes, maintained by our developer experience team; we update them when we add features (like streaming, tool calling). We'll share a sample repo.
[01:52] Marco Ruiz: For production, we'd likely put a gateway/proxy in front of Redwood so we can unify auth and rate limiting. Any recommendations?
[02:00] Liam Patel: Common patterns: 1) call Redwood hosted endpoint directly from backend services with service tokens; 2) put your API gateway in front to handle Okta auth and quota enforcement. For Dedicated or Private, you get VPC peering or private network routing, so the gateway sits in your infra and talks over private links.
[02:19] Aisha Khan: Do you recommend a pass-through proxy or a request-level adapter that handles batching? We have some batching needs to save on tokens.
[02:27] Liam Patel: Batching often happens at the Redwood side via our continuous batching and prefix caching, but you can also batch at your proxy if you want to aggregate very small calls. Keep in mind request semantics for streaming — if you batch user chats you lose per-user latency.
[02:41] Janelle Torres: About LangChain, does your connector preserve streaming and token-level callbacks?
[02:47] Liam Patel: We have examples that support streaming via async iterators in Python; token callbacks are supported in the SDK so LangChain-style chains can receive partial tokens. There's some caveat with LlamaIndex where you often do chunked embedding calls — that works with our embeddings API.
[03:03] Marco Ruiz: What's the rate limits/quotas model for hosted? We need burst handling for promos.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Hosted has account-level quotas and per-key rate limits; we can configure burst allowances. For production scale, Dedicated offers reserved throughput with autoscaling and burst capacity. We can arrange SLOs in the contract.
[03:24] Marco Ruiz: Any hard limits we should plan for?
[03:26] Liam Patel: For hosted, the public rate limits are conservative; if you expect tens of thousands of concurrent requests we encourage Dedicated. For Dedicated we size pools by tokens/sec and concurrency.
[03:37] Janelle Torres: Observability hooks — we use datadog and need tracing across our calls and token-level cost visibility.
[03:44] Liam Patel: We expose request-level metadata in response headers and optional webhooks for logs. Redwood Console provides per-route and model dashboards with latency and token breakdowns. For tracing, you can send OpenTelemetry spans; we have a tracing hook that can propagate trace IDs.
[03:59] Aisha Khan: Is there an agent that ships trace IDs automatically or do we add it in the SDK?
[04:03] Liam Patel: SDK can propagate trace IDs if you pass the context; otherwise your gateway can attach them. For Dedicated/Private you can also forward logs to your S3/Kinesis for custom pipelines.
[04:15] Marco Ruiz: For private deployment — how does VPC peering work? Firewall rules?
[04:20] Maya Chen: For Redwood Private we offer VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. Peering requires CIDR allowances and specific egress rules; we have a runbook. Communication is over mTLS and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[04:34] Janelle Torres: Do you support bring-your-own-HSM?
[04:37] Liam Patel: We integrate with common KMS solutions and can work on HSM options for Private enterprise customers. We'll flag that for the security packet.
[04:45] Aisha Khan: What about data retention and audit logs — we need 7 years for compliance for certain flows.
[04:51] Maya Chen: Audit log retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted has standard retention windows but we offer add-ons for longer retention. We'll include the retention options in the packet.
[05:01] Marco Ruiz: Practical question — our app uses LangChain Agents heavily. How intrusive is switching the underlying provider to Redwood?
[05:08] Liam Patel: Minimal — our LangChain connector is used like any other OpenAI-compatible provider in many cases. There may be small changes for streaming or function calling semantics, but our examples show typical patterns.
[05:23] Janelle Torres: Any known gotchas with LlamaIndex?
[05:26] Liam Patel: LlamaIndex often does many small embedding calls; watch for rate limits in hosted — batching embeddings and using our bulk embedding endpoints or dedicated capacity helps. Also be mindful of tokenization differences if you use custom token limits.
[05:44] Maya Chen: Can we talk about security checklist quickly? SSO, RBAC, SOC2, and audit logs?
[05:49] Aisha Khan: Yeah those are deal-breakers for us.
[05:52] Liam Patel: We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for Dedicated/Private admin consoles, RBAC via the Console, SOC2 Type II for hosted, and audit logs via both Console and webhooks. We'll send the security/compliance pack with specific certificates.
[06:08] Marco Ruiz: On billing/quoting — how does token accounting work with streaming and function calling?
[06:15] Maya Chen: Token accounting is per-token consumed; streaming doesn't change the billing model. For function/tool calls we count input/output tokens as usual. Our pricing sheet will show examples.
[06:27] Janelle Torres: For the pilot — what minimal integration work would we need?
[06:32] Liam Patel: For a hosted pilot: install the Node or Python SDK, wire auth tokens, add a small gateway route to validate Okta tokens, and use LangChain examples. We'll provide a quickstart repo that should take a few days to wire end-to-end.
[06:46] Marco Ruiz: Will you provide load test numbers or a bench harness?
[06:49] Liam Patel: We have benchmark spreadsheets and perf profiles per model; for Dedicated we can run a bench with your workload. We'll run a short perf test as part of PoC scoping.
[07:00] Aisha Khan: Regarding rollouts — can we do canary or A/B between models?
[07:05] Maya Chen: Yes, the rollout system supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallbacks to smaller models if capacity is constrained. That's in Redwood Console under rollouts.
[07:16] Janelle Torres: One more: network egress — if we move tokens to the cloud, do you support VPC endpoints to avoid public egress?
[07:24] Liam Patel: For Private/Dedicated we support private endpoints and peering; hosted currently requires standard TLS endpoints, but customers with strict egress controls often go Dedicated or Private.
[07:36] Marco Ruiz: Any SLA numbers we can expect for Dedicated?
[07:40] Maya Chen: SLA is in the enterprise contract — typical uptime targets and latency SLOs for Dedicated pools. We'll include sample SLA language in the materials.
[07:50] Aisha Khan: If we want to measure token cost per user for the pilot, what's the best way?
[07:55] Liam Patel: Redwood Console shows per-route token breakdowns, and we can give you access to a demo Console to inspect costs. For more granularity we provide request-level metadata so you can attribute tokens to user ids.
[08:09] Janelle Torres: Let's talk about edge cases — what happens if a model goes OOM or the pool becomes constrained?
[08:15] Liam Patel: The runtime has graceful degradation — automatic fallback policies route to compatible model variants, and Continuous KV caching preserves session state. For OOMs we surface errors and metrics to the Console so you can trigger alerts.
[08:29] Marco Ruiz: Ok, that's helpful. Any question from Redwood side?
[08:33] Maya Chen: Does Calypso have regulatory constraints on data residency?
[08:36] Aisha Khan: Not for the pilot; for production some regions will need EU residency.
[08:40] Liam Patel: We have region options for Dedicated and Private. We'll mark EU residency as a must for production track.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Recap / next steps: we'll send pricing, security packet, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, schedule deep dive with Marco's infra team. Any other asks?
[08:59] Janelle Torres: Could you include an example showing streaming chat with LangChain agents and trace propagation?
[09:04] Liam Patel: Yep, we'll add that to the sample repo.
[09:08] Aisha Khan: Please include retention options and HSM row in the packet.
[09:11] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
[09:16] Meeting end.
